propositions: The inbound link differ is ADD-only by construction and never emits removal records when a link is deleted on the peer, while the outbound direction has a removal path, creating an asymmetric synchronization gap

A link deleted in Jira remains on the local ticket indefinitely because no pass walks local deps to detect peer absence, violating the mutation table row 11 oracle that asserts the link should be absent
The apply layer silently drops removal records due to `action != 'add': continue` logic, so even if the differ emitted removals they would not be applied, creating a silent-failure class
Mirroring peer deletions requires distinguishing between a link the peer actually deleted versus one we failed to observe, and comparing current to prior peer state can infer the difference safely

The shipped behavior is local-wins-and-restore: a link deleted in Jira is re-added on the next reconcile pass, which is convergent and loses no local data, and matches how mature tools like Aha! and Asana handle bidirectional link sync
The correct design for future removal implementation requires a per-binding record of what the peer last had, similar to the pattern introduced in change 1296 for parent synchronization
